item.content:encoded:
This is an interesting piece,although I'm not sure yet if I like it. But I strongly disagree with the Neutralized status.

Still to this day, the place resists any attempt at maintenance. The Foundation probably observed extensively the work of the -1s when it was functional, and could at least begin to understand how it is kept. This resistance is still obviously anomalous, and deserves continued research and full containment.

Just because an anomaly ceased to do what it used to do it doesn't necessarily ceases to be anomalous, and the whole Neutralized status breaks it for me.

item.title: That new picture
item.content:encoded:
There's what look to be suspended-ceiling tiles in the upper right of the frame. They strike me as somewhat out-of-period, 55-57 being the era in which the structure was built and the piece overall having what I can only describe as being a pre-70s feel. I dunno, maybe they're evidence of the failed attempts at maintenance/reconstruction that's mentioned?

The picture itself is beautiful, though. The shafts of sunlight in the midst of industrial/commercial decay really gets me. I'd like it to fit, I guess I'm just vague on how it does.

On a distantly related note, how the hell does this not even have +100 yet? That's just not right.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It doesn't follow thru to actual neutralization. Presumably, the violent animatronics eventually wind down entirely like the talking ones, but the article doesn't actually say that.

Sometimes it seems like the description was written when the place was open and then added to as conditions changed, but there are parts where it reads like the whole thing was written retroactively after the place "went out of business". In my head, the Foundation wouldn't write up a procedures to contain an anomaly that was neutralized-on-arrival; so the parts that read that way really don't work for me.

I find nothing wrong with the concept, a decently original take on an old trope. But the execution leaves me cold and I am forced to disagree with the majority opinion, -1.

Edit: Six years later, either the article has changed or my tastes have. Because none of the points above now seem valid, reverse to a +1.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Mr. Funland sat down and let out a heavy sigh, his decision placing a huge burden on his mind. He still couldn't believe that after all these years he simply had to shut down the park. That park was his dream, his legacy! What was he supposed to do from now on? He knew he was going to eventually go back into business, but for what?

Another park? Maybe in the future, but right now it doesn't seem likely.

Books? Eh, he's never really been one for writing.

Toys?

…actually…that's not a bad idea. The toys were one of the most popular elements of the park. Even the most jaded and stoic kids cracked a smile when they laid eyes on a Funland Fantasy Figurine, even if it's charm existed only in their imaginations.

Funland stood up, confident he was on the right path now. Yes! He would start making toys! But not just any toys, oh no! He'd make the most wonderful, most unique toys this world had ever seen, possibly even this universe had ever seen! They would invoke the most basic, most primal elements of whimsy and fantasy into the hearts of children, just as his beloved park once did.

But he couldn't call himself Mr. Funland anymore. It wouldn't flow well on toy labels, and frankly it was just another reminder of a shattered dream that would always drag him back to the past. No! He had to start fresh! He would have to think of something better, something unique. A name that invoked feelings of wonder and entertainment.

Wonder…entertainment…
